title: Statement Regarding the Publication of Reference Rates on Friday, April 3, 2026
summary: The New York Fed announced that SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, and related reference rates will not be published on Friday, April 3, 2026, due to Good Friday and the March Employment Situation release. Settlement of cleared Treasury repo will not be available that day, eliminating two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates. EFFR and OBFR will continue to publish per the New York Fed's holiday schedule.
key_points: No publication of TGCR, BGCR, SOFR, SOFR Averages, or SOFR Index on Friday, April 3, 2026
EFFR and OBFR will be published on April 3, 2026 per the New York Fed's holiday schedule
Settlement of cleared Treasury repo is not scheduled for April 3, eliminating two of three market segments used to calculate Treasury repo reference rates
On Monday April 6, TGCR, BGCR, and SOFR will be published reflecting Thursday April 2 settling transactions maturing Monday April 6
SOFR Averages and Index published April 6 will have a value date of April 6
SIFMA did not recommend a full market closure for U.S. government securities trading, but repo market participants broadly expect to treat April 3 as a holiday
why_it_matters: Market participants relying on SOFR-based products or using SOFR for valuation, margining, or benchmarking need to adjust for a gap in reference rate publication. The absence of cleared repo settlement eliminates most intraday rate discovery, creating a temporary blind spot in overnight funding market metrics.
market_structure_context: This is a scheduled operational notice about reference rate publication arrangements during a market holiday. It highlights the dependency of SOFR on cleared Treasury repo settlement availability and the distinction between government securities trading (which continues) and repo market settlement (which halts).
notes: Source is a brief operational notice from the New York Fed. While relevant to market structure, content is factual with minimal depth. Published March 12, 2026—contemporaneous with TODAY, so not stale. EFFR/OBFR publication on holidays is noted as following New York Fed's own holiday schedule, which may differ from full market closure recommendations.
